root_cause.text: The l2cap_ecred_data_rcv() function in the Bluetooth L2CAP subsystem fails to validate that the received PDU contains at least 2 bytes (L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE) before reading the SDU length via get_unaligned_le16(), leading to an out-of-bounds read when the skb is too short.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state that "l2cap_ecred_data_rcv() reads the SDU length field from skb->data using get_unaligned_le16() without first verifying that skb contains at least L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE (2) bytes. When skb->len is less than 2, this reads past the valid data in the skb." The patch adds a `pskb_may_pull(skb, L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE)` check before the read, mirroring the existing safeguard in the ERTM reassembly path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check before reading SDU length to prevent out-of-bounds access in L2CAP ECRED data reception.
intent_record.what: Added a check with pskb_may_pull() to ensure the skb contains at least L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE bytes before reading the SDU length; if insufficient, sets err to -EINVAL and jumps to the failed label.
intent_record.how: Prevents reading beyond the skb data by verifying the minimum required length before accessing the SDU length field, returning an error if the skb is too short.

grouping_result.intent: Add a length check before reading SDU length to prevent out-of-bounds access in L2CAP ECRED data reception.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly adds a missing length check for L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE before reading the SDU length, which precisely addresses the root cause of the out-of-bounds read vulnerability in l2cap_ecred_data_rcv().

candidates.rationale: This statement reads 2 bytes from skb->data without ensuring that skb->len is at least L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE, resulting in out-of-bounds access when the skb is too short.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement reads 2 bytes from the beginning of the skb data buffer to obtain the SDU length, but does not verify that the skb contains at least 2 bytes (L2CAP_SDULEN_SIZE). When the received PDU is too short, the read overruns the packet buffer, causing an out-of-bounds read.
